notes: Web search was already used up for the session (the tool reported 200 of 200) before this part began, so no search was run for any of the 30 candidates. Everything here was read directly with the kit's own User-Agent, robots.txt obeyed: the campaign sites the candidates filed, the governments' own pages, the Legislative Reference Library, the University of Minnesota's regents pages and its election archive. A campaign site nobody filed could not be looked for, so a missing website is not proof that none exists.

Nothing found, and no way to search further: Brandon Van Dover (no election-archive page; no party unit site found), David De La Hunt, Danny Geronsin, Naomi Larson, Judy Onken LaBoda, Daryl Wicklund, Holly Menke, Vincent "Vinny" Jay Peterson, Luke Christian, Joel Hollerich, Patti Johnson, Gwen Ulland, Nicole Karch, Emily J. Froehle. The governments' own pages show that Geronsin (Martin County names Jaime Bleess in District 2), Larson (Kittson County names Loren Younggren in District 3), Onken LaBoda (Murray County names Jackie Meier in District 4), Menke (Sherburne County names Michelle Ashe as Recorder), Peterson (not on Otsego's council page), Christian (St. Cloud names Hudda Ibrahim in the 3rd Ward), Hollerich, Johnson and Karch (not on their districts' board pages) do not hold the seat they seek today.

Out of reach and not worked around: www.co.hubbard.mn.us is closed to scripts by robots.txt (David De La Hunt); www.co.roseau.mn.us answered with a Radware CAPTCHA page (Daryl Wicklund); mncourts.gov answers 403 (Emily J. Froehle); the East Grand Forks district's board page draws its names by script (Gwen Ulland); dfl.org and Wikipedia's API shut out Claude's agents in robots.txt, so nothing is cited from them; mngop.com's nominees page draws its list by script. Mower County's Sheriff's Office page does not name the sheriff, so Steven Sandvik has no official page here and his office rests on his own campaign site.

No party's own endorsement page could be found for anyone in this part, so there is no endorsed_by entry. Robyn Gulley's own site says "Proudly DFL & Labor Endorsed" (kept as own_words). The Senate District 55 DFL's site (sd55dfl.org) does not name Hunter Cantrell on the pages that could be read. Bobbie Harder's and Sebastian Stoss's endorsement sections show images only.
Bobbie Harder is a sitting legislator with a record page, so only her website is recorded (her site also says she served two terms as a Sibley County Commissioner).

Nicole Mitchell: the same person as the former state senator: her campaign site says she grew up and lives in Woodbury and speaks of her legislative work from 2023 to 2025, and the Library's record gives Senate District 47, Woodbury, a term from January 2, 2023 to July 25, 2025 (it records that she resigned) and says she announced a run for the Woodbury City Council in 2026. The Library's page carries other details that are not collected here.

Hunter Cantrell: his own site says he served in the Minnesota House from 2019 to 2021, matching the Library's record (term of office January 7, 2019 to January 3, 2021). Bradley Dahl is written Brad Dahl by the City of Buffalo. Brian Lutes: co.wright.mn.us/attorney redirects to the address given.
